notes.title: Arrows and Aiming: Damage Zones
notes.content: [h2]Greetings, warriors![/h2][p]Not every arrow strikes with the same force. In Shadow of the Road, ranged combat is governed by Damage Zones - a system that makes positioning and distance just as important as going first.[/p][previewyoutube="ZBaSMncptJI;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Every ranged weapon has an Attack Distance, divided into two distinct range bands:[/p][p]	[b]Close[/b] – the optimal range, limited by the dotted line on the combat grid. Shots landed here are most effective.[/p][p]	[b]Far[/b] – the extended range, beyond the dotted line on the combat grid. Attacks that connect to far targets lose a portion of their power.[/p][p][/p][p]The battlefield grid highlights these Damage Zones dynamically, letting you judge at a glance whether you’re striking at full strength. It is of some note, that targets outside of your Attack Distance cannot be hit.[/p][p][/p][h3]What's the difference?[/h3][p]Inside the Close range all ranged attacks strike with deadly precision and inflict their full damage.[/p][p]Attacks will still connect with the targets in the Far range, but will have their damage output reduced by 25% - especially noticeable on Critical Hits, which makes the bow-wielding Akira very sad. Sometimes, the difference is enough to decide between a KO and a target left standing.[/p][p][/p][h3]Tradition vs Progress[/h3][p]Most Bows have their Attack Distance split 50%/50% between Close and Far Damage Zones, while most Guns keep their effectiveness further into long ranges, and have a 75%/25% ratio. Hooray for progress?[/p][p][/p][h3]Why do Witches cackle?[/h3][p]Because not all attacks are bound by these rules. Magical abilities are only limited by their Attack Distance and ignore Damage Zones entirely, remaining effective across the battlefield. Where an arrow weakens over distance, a spell hits with the same force no matter how far it flies![/p][p][/p][h3]In the right place, at the right time[/h3][p]The Damage Zone system rewards tactical awareness - not just who you target, but also where you stand, and when you move: do you move your fighter closer and take full damage, or do you delay and take a weakened extreme range shot first?[/p][p]While a misplaced step can put you into the Close range of an enemy marksman, a clever shove can force that same marksman into reduced damage on your back line. Fighters like Ishida can displace enemies, changing the math of shots fired.[/p][p]Adapt to the shifting lines of the battlefield to excel at combat in Shadow of the Road: weigh risks against rewards, plan your moves two steps ahead, and strike from the distance that suits your tactics best.[/p][p][/p][p]Join our community at Discord: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/c4c51a7246abc6e04e52aef35cc833f2e90045aa.png"][/img] [/p][p]And other platforms! notes.title: Dynamic Turn Order
notes.content: [h2]Hello warriors![/h2][p]Are you tired of turn-based combat growing stale by round 2, following the same routine of enemies go -> party goes -> rinse, repeat? Well then, you're in luck! Instead of rounds following a fixed pattern, Shadow of the Road keeps things fresh by offering a constantly evolving Timeline.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="5EKHOSVhTFA;full"][/previewyoutube][h3]What is the Timeline?[/h3][p]Every character in combat, whether an ally or an enemy, has an Initiative value.  Initiative determines their place in the turn order queue that is called the Timeline.[/p][p]The higher the character's Initiative is, the sooner they can act, and the more to the left they're placed on the Timeline.[/p][p]If two or more characters have the same Initiative, the game decides randomly between them. Once someone takes a turn, they’re moved behind the others with equal Initiative - keeping things fair and varied. Simple enough at first glance, but the Timeline evolves rapidly in play.[/p][h3]What affects the Timeline?[/h3][p]Initiative values shift mid-combat, meaning the turn order on the Timeline isn’t locked, and it's constantly updated in response to a plethora of factors:[/p][p]	- Every damaging attack inflicts Distraction, which reduces the target’s Initiative on a successful hit;[/p][p]	- Some abilities (like Dazzle) apply longer-term effects that lower Initiative over multiple turns, making it harder for affected units to recover their tempo;[/p][p]	- The team that initiates combat gets a temporary Initiative boost, rewarding careful planning and positioning;[/p][p]	- Some characters have passive perks that resist Initiative loss, or gain extra Initiative under specific circumstances.[/p][p]This keeps the battlefield fluid and compels the player to take into account the consequences of everyone's actions when planning.[/p][p]If a character’s Initiative drops below 0 at any time, their current turn ends immediately, regardless of how many Action or Movement Points they had left: a well-timed hit can cancel a unit’s entire turn, before they get to act! That means, planning your attacks around the Timeline is just as important as damage output.[/p][p]A character’s Initiative value resets as soon as they finish their turn. However, there's a catch: if they take damage before their next turn starts (say, from someone still acting in the current round), that new Initiative can still be lowered — potentially pushing them even further down in the Timeline.[/p][h3]Navigating the Timeline[/h3][p]The Timeline bar at the top of the screen shows:[/p][p]	- Portraits of the characters with upcoming turns;[/p][p]	- Their names;[/p][p]	- Their current Initiative values.[/p][p]The bar is split into Current Round and Next Round, letting you see who’s acting now and who’s up next. It updates in real-time as characters act, take damage, or die.[/p][p]This system rewards deeper tactics, rather than a raw, by the numbers approach. For example, a player skilled at navigating the Timeline can delay enemies to interrupt their strongest units, or pull allies forward on the Timeline to protect an objective.[/p][h3]So, how to master the Timeline?[/h3][p]You can go and try it for yourself - the Demo for Shadow of the Road is available right now, and it's free! Let us know what you think in the comments, and don't forget to fill out the Demo survey - we’re listening.[/p][p]Just remember:[/p][p]A true samurai is never late, just like a wizard. Nor is he early. He arrives precisely when he means to.[/p][p]Join our community at Discord: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/c4c51a7246abc6e04e52aef35cc833f2e90045aa.png"][/img] [/p][p]And other platforms! notes.title: Alpha Survey Results
notes.content: [h1]Greetings, honourable warriors and wandering vagabonds![/h1][p][/p][h2]A Perspective on Players[/h2][p]Shadow of the Road has cocluded the Open Alpha stage, and we're immensely grateful for the passion and dedication you've shown as you’ve plunged headfirst into its world. The feedback we've received from you has been [i]invaluable[/i]. It’s exhilarating to see how players from all over the globe have taken to our game, and we’re thrilled to discuss some of the key takeaways from the results of our latest community survey.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/c2e90a39ee7d613e69eecb18ff20d29276672e87.png"][/img]We’ve also seen a wide range of player ages, with an overwhelming majority fairly evenly distributed between 25 and 44 years old.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/130b2e93b214ce064be28edd69aaf97bb5094eba.png"][/img][/p][p]In line with the CRPG, Strategy and Action-Adventure genres, which are the top-3 among our players, 91% of the samurai who took time to participate in this survey identify as male. The battlefields are, indeed, harsh places - but there is more to Shadow of the Road than mere tactical conflict, and we'll be sure to communicate it clearer moving onwards. Tell your sisters, share it with your wives and mothers! We'll be happy to see them and share our stories.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/b9ce2e0a78f9d0c3d71a823322992474c9ea5c8d.png"][/img][/p][p]We also noticed a significant crossover in game preferences, with a large portion of you also enjoying action titles like Ghost of Tsushima [b](49.3%)[/b], Nioh/Nioh2 [b](35.7%)[/b], and Sekiro [b](42%)[/b]. It’s no surprise that the historical themes and fluid combat have resonated with fans of these franchises. Over [b]72%[/b] of survey participants [b]completed the Alpha,[/b] showing the enthusiasm for getting hands-on with the game early and contributing to its refinement.[/p][p][/p][h2]SotR's Satisfying Statistics[/h2][p]Combat and gameplay: tough, yet rewarding. One of the most significant areas we focused on was encounter difficulty. We’ve received a wealth of feedback, and it seems the challenge level is just right for most players, earning a [b]4.11 out of 5[/b] satisfaction rating for the combat system.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/af38ef3b3ed50a18571e56442235b4cdc02dce48.png"][/img]From the design perspective, the visual spectacle of the game's combat was clear enough for [b]85% of Alpha participants[/b], with only occasional issues needing further ironing out. We're particularily glad to find out that the unusual continuous initiative Timeline was quickly and easily understood by [b]more than 81%[/b] of our players, and the rest of the combat UI was found intuitive and easy to navigate [b]by 87.3%[/b]. [/p][p]Despite the inventory UI being perfectly serviceable, it seems we’ve touched on a quirky issue! [b]Only about 65% of players have used consumable items[/b], ergo, a significant number of respondents expressed a certain… caution when it came to using them, despite the evidence suggesing there being more than enough supplies to go around. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Four out of every five[/b] players found the dialogue UI both convenient and pleasing. And we're proud of the approval scores for that dialogue UI's contents across the board: interfaces can be polished, but your appreciation of our creative efforts is what truly matters! [b]More than 60% of you became interested in learning the Japanese names and terminology highlighted in the dialogues and texts, with explanations of their meanings provided via tooltips[/b]. The partial Japanese VO [b](76.6%)[/b] and cutscenes [b](71.3%)[/b], designed to bring an additional layer of immersion to the world, were also highly praised, with most of you giving them the thumbs up.[/p][p][/p][p]The skill upgrade system was another pleasant surprise, with most of you - [b]84%[/b], - appreciating its clarity. And while there's room for growth for the progression system's satisfaction factor, the variety of playstyles and story choices proves engaging - reflected in your [b]4 out of 5[/b] overall score for interest in experimenting with different abilities and narrative paths.[/p][p][/p][p]Every journey starts somewhere, and those first steps are often the most important one can take. So, either our players have unmatched expertise, or we have crushed the tutorial first try! However, despite being exceptionally informative, the tutorial scores [b]3.86/5[/b] on the Not-Bothersome scale as of now. Which is nice, but it means we're not going to get too full of ourselves:  hundreds of you - a third of all respontents! - have left a wealth of comments and tips on how we can furhter improve this foundational experience. We are immensely grateful for the feedback you provide us with, and the time you dedicate to playing the game and making it better![img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/a3e7cb7b1e7d2117e1258605a7f1e99af1a08312.png"][/img]The skill upgrade system was another pleasant surprise, with most of you - [b]84%[/b], - appreciating its clarity. And while there's room for growth for the progression system's satisfaction factor, the variety of playstyles and story choices proves engaging - reflected in your [b]4 out of 5[/b] overall score for interest in experimenting with different abilities and narrative paths.[/p][p][/p][p]And of course, when it comes to immersion, we can't overlook the musical score - accompanying players on their journeys and keeping the tension high during combat. With a [b]4.1 out of 5[/b] rating, we're truly grateful for the appreciation you've shown.[/p][p][/p][h2]Roaming the Realms[/h2][p]You’ve also shown great interest for exploring the Shadow of the Road's world and setting. We’ve heard you loud and clear - the majority of players [b](70%)[/b] have experienced the wanderlust, looking forwards to uncovering secrets, takckling side quests, taking in the vistas and collecting the hidden lore scattered throughout the world.[/p][p][/p][p]The journal system, which keeps track of quests, lore entries, and world-building notes, was useful to most players who chose to engage with it. More than half of the Open Alpha participants found the journal to be a useful tool.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/f2a01b766304648263bfed4c2e2f7a7cfeae37eb.png"][/img]Worldbuilding has been a particular highlight at [b]4.4/5[/b], and we understand that the players take the time to explore character backgrounds, hidden documents, and in-game lore. This has helped enhance the players' understanding of the larger conflict unfolding and immerse them in the game even further.[/p][h2]Companions, Choices & Charisma[/h2][p]From the generous score of [b]4.4 out of 5[/b] It’s clear that the narrative-driven design has struck a chord with our Open Alpha auditory.[/p][p]And so, we've finally come to the meat on the bones of any party-based RPG. We couldn’t possibly progress any more without acknowledging the cast, the stalwart companions who stand by each other's side through thick and thin. Without further ado, let's dive deeper into these character impressions![/p][h2][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/3513c115806c465086bab1c8304063f130c386c3.png"][/img]Delights and Dislikes[/h2][p]Time to wrap it up. Here's a blitz round of some final sneak peeks into what is favoured and what is reviled![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/65cd95dfe56c95cfda0573ae66e152efee91a106.png"][/img]As we look at the feedback and statistics gracefully shared with us by the Open Alpha pioneers, one thing is clear: your passion for Shadow of the Road is inspiring. You’ve offered us so many insights into what’s working, what could use a little tweaking, and what has truly captured your imaginations. From combat to exploration, companion interactions to worldbuilding, it’s all about making sure that the journey to come is as enjoyable and rewarding as possible.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/4412ae26428e2c01257228d3399d2f322dd630e8.png"][/img][/p][p][b]4.2 out of 5[/b] is a great result, but there's yet a lot to improve - thanks to you. We hope this final score captures the essence of the survey results, in the same spirit as you've shared with us.[/p][p]Thanks again for your continued support and participation in shaping this game. Stay tuned for further updates, and be prepared for new adventures, deeper storylines, and more thrilling challenges. The battle is far from over - there’s much more to discover.[/p][p][/p][p]Until next time, stay strong, keep exploring, and remember: [i]it's not about the destination, it's about the journey![/i][/p][p][/p][p]Join our community at Discord: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/c4c51a7246abc6e04e52aef35cc833f2e90045aa.png"][/img] [/p][p]And other platforms!  [/p][p]📍 [b][url="https://www.facebook.com/shadowoftheroad"]Facebook[/url][/b]  [/p][p]📍 [b][url="https://x.com/sotr_game"]X (Twitter)[/url][/b]  [/p][p]📍 [b][url="https://www.instagram.com/sotr_game/"]Instagram[/url][/b]  [/p][p]📍 [b][url="https://www.youtube.com/@anotheranglegames"]Youtube[/url][/b][/p][p]   [/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1173980/Shadow_of_the_Road/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Break It Down: Crafting Chaos on the Battlefield!
notes.content:
In the midst of the conflict between traditional mysticism and steampunk progress, the battlefield of Shadow of the Road is as dynamic as the warriors who tread it. For you, honorable samurai, understanding the intricacies of the destructible environment is key to mastering both strategy and surprise on the field.

[h1]Unleashing Destruction[/h1]

Every object in the battlefield can be a tool of chaos when wielded wisely. Most of the surroundings — be they wooden barrels or stone boulders — have their own endurance, determined by their size and the material from which they are made. A nimble strike along an object’s line, or a forceful passage by a large character, can shatter these constructs. When you engage an enemy in your line of sight, you have the power to attack through these breakable barriers, distributing damage between your foe and the obstacle — all without sacrificing your precious Movement Points.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/EKiXon5.gif[/img]

[i]Imagine the battlefield as a living canvas: each shattered object is a stroke of your strategic brilliance. Whether you’re dodging enemy blows or setting up your next devastating attack, every debris can play a part in your victory.[/i]

[h1]The Explosive Edge[/h1]

Beyond the standard objects, a particular set of items awaits those ready to embrace explosive chaos. Gunpowder crates are unique to ENC-affiliated areas. Unlike traditional Japanese armaments, these volatile crates add a modern twist to the ancient art of warfare.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/clsxXwm.gif[/img]

These crates remain inert until their predetermined damage threshold is met. Depending on the weapon — be it the swift slice of a katana or the rapid burst of a rifle — the speed of their explosive reaction may vary. But one fact remains constant: once destroyed, these crates will unleash a powerful blast, damaging all within its circular reach. For a true warrior, the timing and positioning of such explosions can turn the tide of battle in an instant. 

[h1]Stay Connected with the Community[/h1]

As you continue your journey through the dynamic world of Shadow of the Road, make sure you stay connected for the latest updates and insights. Follow our social media channels on

and join our vibrant community on Discord.

These platforms not only keep you informed about exciting new developments and community events, but they also serve as your ultimate guide to mastering the art of chaos on the battlefield.
In conclusion, every shattered barrier and every explosive surprise is a testament to your strategy and spirit as a samurai warrior.

notes.title: Let’s talk about the Initiative System…
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/119bc4fd0ec7073497c09f23726bf5a6a9ef3753.png[/img]

[h1]Samurai Warriors![/h1]

Recently, we treated you to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1173980/announcements/detail/3732977475613248390]an interview with our sound magician[/url], and today we're bringing you a devlog straight from the heart of [b]our game development process[/b]!

Have you ever heard of an initiative system? It's an incredibly vital component in many turn-based RPGs! And the situation is [b]no different in Shadow of the Road[/b], where it plays a fundamental role. In simple words -  its primary task is to determine the order in which characters get to make their moves.

Let us share a bit of the history of [b]how this system has evolved in our game[/b]… 

[h2]In the past…[/h2]

At first, we had a [b]very “XCOM-like” approach[/b] where players could make moves with all characters in any order (and multiple times within their turn, using available action/movement points). In other words, the player would switch between characters, take actions, end their turn, and after that the game would switch to AI which would act similarly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/e2e05ad642dfe6ab8058466a810637d1592fb13c.png[/img]

We showcased this combat system [b]at PAX in 2020[/b]. And while it served its purpose, we felt that our game needed something more… Something deeper! We needed a system that would allow players to anticipate enemy moves, analyze situations, and have full influence on what is happening on the battlefield!

[h2]So now! [/h2]

The current iteration of the system [b]draws its inspiration from samurai battles[/b], where it's crucial to observe everything and make decisions that significantly impact the course of the clash.

[b]The core of this mechanic revolves around character initiative. [/b]

All characters participating in the battle are [b]sorted based on their initiative values[/b] and the one with the highest value starts the whole action. Default initiative values are predefined, but can change as the game develops. Several factors influence the status, such as an initiative penalty for taking damage and side effects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/1c290d04a129b29f061505642629f140dccdc40e.png[/img]

By introducing this system, we were able to incorporate [b]more combat mechanics[/b] that enhance its depth. 

The main innovation here is [b]delayed attacks[/b]!

These attacks are more effective, but carry a risk of failure. A delayed attack is carried out as a new element on the timeline. So the character initiating it cannot move and automatically ends their turn. If they are attacked before executing the attack, it will be interrupted.

This system also operates in rounds, with [b]each unit making one move per round[/b]. 

[h2]Unfortunately… [/h2]

Introduced changes also have some drawbacks that make this solution less than perfect. Notable issues include:

⚔️ Delaying attacks by a fixed value can lead to situations where nobody on the battlefield can counter or interrupt them. We attempted to solve this by delaying attacks based on factors like the number of characters, but this fix won’t be good enough.

⚔️ Time axis shifts are inconsistent. We couldn't find a solution that would allow us to predictably and fairly move a unit, for example, to the next round. A character that received a high amount of damage would end up at the end of the queue in a given round.

⚔️ The chance of having a negative initiative value. After receiving a sufficient amount of damage, a unit might have a negative initiative value, which isn't considered a valid value. While we could theoretically try to soften this effect by increasing base values, it wouldn't eliminate the entire problem.

But guess what…? These issues prompted us to work on another version of the system! 

[h2]What the future holds…[/h2]

Treat this like a small sneak peek, but… 

In previous systems, the gameplay was divided into rounds in which action points and character movement reset at the beginning of each subsequent turn. The new system will have an additional dimension, and we will be abandoning the concept of rounds. However, we don't intend to reveal too much just yet, as there's more to come. 

[b]Rest assured, everything is continuously evolving![/b]

[h2]Stay tuned![/h2]

To stay in the loop regarding our progress, come join our Discord community! And once again, thank you for being a part of this incredible journey!

notes.title: Meet the Team - Sound Designer 🎶
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/69a63b5edc3c88749dc0b8de4e6287d53ee32fad.png[/img]

We've got a real treat for you today - [b]an interview with our sound designer[/b], Kostek Antonowicz (check out his [url=https://www.instagram.com/kostek.sound/]Instagram[/url])! Sound is of great importance to us, so we were looking for someone whose passion would allow us to translate it into the game.

Are you curious about who's behind the magical audio in Shadow of the Road? No need to beat around the bush - allow us to introduce...

[h3]Who are you?[/h3]

Hey, I'm Kostek, I came to Earth to make some noise.

[h3]What are your responsibilities in the team working on Shadow of the Road?[/h3]

I am responsible for audio. I create sound designs and implement them - first into Wwise and later into Unity. Additionally, I collaborate with a musician to create interactive music.

[h3]Which software do you use?[/h3]

I use game engines like Unity or Unreal, and sound middleware like Fmod or Wwise. For sound creation, I use Cubase and Ableton.

[h3]How would you define “video game music”?[/h3]

Video game music is the primary carrier of emotions. It's a universal language that doesn't require translation, allowing creators to shape how players perceive the game world and gameplay at any moment.

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀    [img]https://media.giphy.com/media/GMC6gi4AglqLf476wJ/giphy.gif[/img]
[i][url=https://www.instagram.com/kostek.sound/]Full video on Kostek's Instagram[/url][/i]

[h3]What role, in your opinion, does the music play in Shadow of the Road?[/h3]

The music in Shadow of the Road, in addition to fulfilling basic requirements, places a strong emphasis on interactivity. For example, it incorporates changes in feelings and character of the music based on dialogue choices. It adapts as you explore the game world or encounter danger, creating a dynamic and immersive musical experience.

[h3]What guides you when creating the audio layer for Shadow of the Road?[/h3]

When creating audio for Shadow of the Road, my primary focus is on the concept of immersion. I want players to navigate the game world not only through their eyes, but also through their ears. Sometimes, while walking along the path, you might hear something that catches your attention, or you might get startled by a sound and decide that you're not ready to go in that direction. 

I have a deep appreciation for the ambient sounds of nature and previously nonexistent creatures in games, as they provide room for creativity and interpretation. I have the opportunity to work on all of this and more with Another Angle Games.

[h3]What sets the sound in Shadow of the Road apart from other games?[/h3]

At a certain point, the audio in most games can be comparable. In Shadow of the Road, we placed a greater emphasis than usual on environmental sounds that allow for deeper immersion and the ability to differentiate areas. We are giving them a distinct audio character. Forests should feel mysterious, dense, and full of life, while other dimensions should sound demonic and ominous. The goal is to create a unique audio identity for each area.

[h3]What is the most challenging aspect of your job?[/h3]

Finding the balance between individual sounds. On one hand, sounds need to be clear and attention-grabbing, but on the other, there are times when audio should step back and make room for something else. I also strive to find unconventional solutions to make sure that the designs, even if they are abstract, are clear and intuitive for the player.

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   [img]https://media.giphy.com/media/o4RZPWMmeM8S1fSwGh/giphy.gif[/img]
  [i][url=https://www.instagram.com/kostek.sound/]Full video on Kostek's Instagram[/url][/i]

[h3]Which aspect of your work are you most proud of (at this stage)?[/h3]

The most satisfying moment is when I can experience the game I've worked on from the perspective of a player. I feel proud that everything is cohesive, and I can spend a lot of time in the game just walking around and listening. 

[h3]Why is it  worth waiting for Shadow of the Road?[/h3]

I had the opportunity to observe the team's dedication and the progress of development - there's no doubt that this title is going to be fantastic. It's a massive game being made with heart.

[h3]What is your favorite Yokai?[/h3]

My favorite Yokai is Kazenbō, because sometimes when I'm hungry, I make a scene just like him. He's not threatening, but people are afraid of him. :D 

[h3]Thank you! [/h3]

[h1]Warriors![/h1] 

Hello again! In today's post we want to shed some light on the creative process behind Shadow of the Road and its evolution as a representative of the tactical RPG genre. 

We'd like to delve into the genesis of the idea, our approach towards the environment, and the significance of skills. So, without further ado, [b]let’s see where it all started[/b]! 

[h2]Our passion for this genre runs deep…[/h2]

…From hours spent battling in turn-based strategies to the immersive worlds of games like [b]Final Fantasy, X-COM, Unholy War, Front Mission, Temple of Elemental Evil, Etherlords[/b], and many more. Years ago, we used to play together some of the finest representatives of the genre – for example, the Fallout series (especially Fallout: Tactics).

One could say that the opportunity to create a world that would hold as much significance for players as in the titles we mentioned is almost like a dream come true. We’re sure that many of [b]you could understand it very well[/b]! 

[h2]Moving on! [/h2]

Some time ago we mentioned the verticality of certain levels. It’s important, but that's not the only interesting aspect in the context of the environment! Soon you'll find special interactive zones that add depth to the gameplay and [b]maximize immersion[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/00fc87d03b93876adb1e5b91bce7b363d5c39249.png[/img]

For example - imagine scenarios where you're ablaze and [b]you can jump into the water[/b] to extinguish the flames, or have the ability to ignite oil for strategic advantage. Sounds great, huh? We want the environment to be a backdrop to the narrative events and a part of them at the same time.

[h2]What about skills?[/h2]

[b]Skills are a cornerstone[/b] of the tactical RPG genre, and it’s no different in our game. They're not just decorative – they shape the core of the gameplay. Our focus lies heavily on the tactical depth within them. Well, it’s safe to say that we have plenty of intriguing aspects planned, but we'll save those juicy details for future updates… ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/63f106e1fedf2e538405502470c85e768de18c14.png[/img]

Certainly,[b] it's worth mentioning the Yokai system[/b], which will be almost a fundamental aspect for us. Summoning them to add a new dimension to battles will be something unique in the realm of other tactical RPG games. The system might share some similarities with Guardian Forces from Final Fantasy VIII, but there will be many more differences than resemblances. We can't wait to present it to you - you’ll love it! 

[h2]More to come! [/h2]

Before we wrap up, we want to extend a heartfelt thank you for sticking with us and supporting the whole development process. Your active participation in our journey is invaluable, and your passion fuels our dedication to [b]making Shadow of the Road the best it can be[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/a9488f261184aadfedbac9b587c9f6c736bebe11.png[/img]

[h1]Hello, Warriors![/h1]

It's nice to be writing to you again! Firstly, we are grateful for your support and continuous feedback. We truly appreciate your patience as we worked through each step of the development process. [b]We’re getting closer[/b]!

Today we'll delve into a crucial aspect of Shadow of the Road - the environment. We're well aware of its significance in turn-based RPGs, and [b]it's a paramount element in our game[/b] as well.

[h2]Beautiful World[/h2]

As the game is set in Japan, [b]during the fall of the Empire's feudal era in 1868[/b], the surroundings are reminiscent of the 19th-century Land of the Rising Sun. To create an environment that truly captures it, we had to dig through loads of pics from back then. 

Luckily, [b]some photos have survived the passage of time[/b]. We found pictures of rich people, villagers in their settlements, ports, markets, bridges, and even abandoned castles… But we didn't stop there – we also checked out artwork from earlier times, showing how they built temporary fortifications! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/6a6ad83f4c753cb05ceb59b206a7a00ccc17a0c2.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/615cf46fc8b29065a72314d61cf80470797dcc62.png[/img]
[i]Source: oldphotosjapan.com[/i]

And hey, we couldn't miss the opportunity to draw inspiration from legendary movies like Akira Kurosawa's "Ran" and the [b]whole collection of "Rurouni Kenshin"[/b] movies by Keishi Otomo. Have you watched them? 

[h2]Don't expect a monotonous environment! [/h2]

Shadow of the Road [b]will take you on a journey[/b] to diverse locations, ranging from underground cave systems to open meadows, from serene monasteries to dangerous forests. Each of them is very distinct from another. All offer diverse experience, opportunities, and atmosphere.

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   [img]https://media.giphy.com/media/OVl1S4DJioei83RKCZ/giphy.gif[/img]

Keep in mind that the environment will influence the flow of combat. With such varied terrain, certain characters may gain advantage, and attacks that seem impossible in other settings, can suddenly be effortlessly executed. Adding to the immersion, [b]some elements of the environment will be destructible[/b], making every encounter more dynamic and engaging.

[b]Speaking of that[/b] - we wrote more about utilizing the terrain in combat in our previous devlog, so if you haven't read it yet - we encourage you to catch up!

[h2]Seek and you shall find[/h2]

Moreover, [b]we didn't want our world to feel empty[/b], so you'll come across numerous collectibles along the way. These items will significantly impact your characters. Moreover, you will be able to find shrines, providing a boost to your abilities too.

We believe that a [b]true warrior must be vigilant[/b], so keep your eyes wide open - not only to admire the beauty of the surrounding nature. We want to reward those who will stray from the beaten path while exploring the world of Shadow of the Road.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/e02cca6c2c70e09fa0a426dcb0e7934f6164bf06.png[/img]

[h1]Warriors! [/h1]

Today, we’d like to delve into the fascinating [b]fusion of steampunk and Japanese culture[/b]. These two seemingly different elements come together in a remarkable way, creating an incredible atmosphere that keeps us hooked (and hopefully you too!).

[h2]Let's talk a bit about steampunk and its origins…[/h2]

[b]Steampunk is a subgenre of science fiction[/b] that combines futuristic technology with Victorian aesthetics. It's all about that retro vibe, with steam-powered machinery and a touch of industrial revolution. It's a style that has captured the imagination of many and has become a beloved theme in various forms of media. 

There were many books, TV shows, and even games (for example BioShock, Dishonored, or Final Fantasy VI) created in this genre. We're sure that, to some extent, [b]you've already encountered steampunk[/b], whether consciously or not. But never before in the form that we intend to present it in our game!

In the world of Shadow of the Road, the responsibility of bringing steampunk to Japan [b]lies with EMC[/b] (a mysterious British conglomerate with unclear intentions).

Initially, the idea of blending these seemingly contrasting atmospheres seemed risky to us. After all, Japan, the Land of the Rising Sun, evokes an entirely different imagery. [b]It's all about that Zen vibe[/b] – peace, balance, spirituality, and chill.

However, it's precisely this unexpected combination that [b]makes the world of Shadow of the Road so captivating[/b]. It immerses you deeply and leaves you craving for more. You want to navigate through the next stages of what seems so unassuming, believe us. 

[h2]Join us![/h2] 

We are confident that during the upcoming testing phase (and by the way, we encourage you to join our [url=bit.ly/SOTR_Discord]Discord[/url] to participate), you'll also get to experience the feeling we're talking about. 

We encourage you to [b]keep following the game's development[/b] on Discord, Twitter, Facebook, and right here - on Steam. Moreover, if you have any questions, don't hesitate to reach out. We'll respond as quickly as possible and with great pleasure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/52b11b54da0a92f2eab553f0475c786423d5b13f.png[/img]

[h1]Warriors![/h1]

To kick things off, we would like to express our gratitude for your companionship on the journey of developing Shadow of the Road. Stay with us and stay tuned - [b]we’re still progressing[/b]!

[b]The Yokai are an integral part of the game[/b], one of its pillars. We understand that not everyone may be familiar with who or what these creatures are, so we've decided to provide some insight.

Yokai are fascinating beings [b]deeply rooted in Japanese folklore[/b] and mythology. They encompass a wide range of supernatural creatures, from mischievous spirits to powerful entities. Yokai can be seen as a collective term for a wide range of beings, including spirits, monsters, demons, and ghosts.

Each of them has its unique characteristics and origins, making them a captivating part of the world. When it comes to categorizing Yokai, [b]there are several ways to go about it[/b]. One common approach is based on their characteristics and behavior (e.g. Oni, Kappa, Yurei…). However, we don't want to spoil their exact role in the game's storyline. 

Rest assured, though, that [b]you will come across Yokai on more than one occasion[/b]. Their presence will add an extra layer of mystery and excitement to your path in the game. You will be able to control some of them and to figure out their intentions and background. Intrigued, huh? 

[h2]To wrap it up… [/h2]

Shadow of the Road is an ambitious project, and the scale of the work done for it is appropriately large. The entire team worked restlessly to bring it to fruition and our silent period comes with all sorts of cool milestones and achievements to show for it. 

We have completed character dialogues for the entire first half of the game. We have diversified the game with levels set in gloomy underground passages and treacherous uncharted forests. And of course, put significant work into the characters you will encounter as you play Shadow of the Road!

Let’s put a number to some of the things we’ve wrapped up as of late:
- Wrote roughly 50k words of dialogues and other in-game texts; 
- Finished modeling over 30 different characters and enemies;
- Finished 4 levels with 13 more in the pipeline and waiting to be braved.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.content:
[b]Q: Are you planning to release Shadow of the Road on platforms other than PC?[/b]
*A:* There are indeed some plans related to console versions of SotR, but for now our top priority is the PC version. 

[b]Q: What is the price of the game going to be?[/b]
*A:* It will be decided later on, but we think that the base price will be somewhere around $30.

[b]Q: Is there going to be a multiplayer option?[/b]
*A:* Probably not, for sure not at the time of the initial release. We have done some tests and even made a playable multiplayer prototype but for now we are focusing on a single-player campaign.

[b]Q: Are you working on macOS and Linux versions?[/b]
*A:* Due to some technical limitations and performance issues on those platforms it is very unlikely that SotR will appear on macOS and/or Linux, although we have prepared a MacOS version for internal testing purposes. If we notice high user demand for those versions we will however take it into consideration.

[b]Q: Are you planning any open/closed tests?[/b]
*A:* Yes, definitely. We are unable to handle all the QA by ourselves so we will rely heavily on the support of our community.

[b]Q: Are you planning to release a demo?[/b]
*A:* Yes, but we don't know at what phase it’s going to happen. It can be tied to various events that depend on Steam.

[b]Q: Is the game going to be available in Early Access?[/b]
*A:* We haven't decided yet if will it be hard launched or put into Early Access. There is plenty of work to be done before even considering release in any form.

[b]Q: Who is working on this? / Who are you, guys?  [/b]
*A:* We are a small independent studio Another Angle Games based in Warsaw. This is our first big title so we rely heavily on our community. We hope that our players will have a significant impact on the development process.

[b]Q: I have a suggestion. How can I pass it on to the dev team?[/b]
*A:* If it is a game related suggestion you can submit it to a channel on our Discord server and let others put it to vote. Once in a while we dig through the suggestions and select those with positive feedback from our community and put them onto our roadmap.

[b]Q: Where can I find the latest updates?[/b]
*A:* We post the important updates to the Steam Community but you can find more internal content on our Discord server. We also run SotR profiles on various social media platforms:
• on Twitter: https://twitter.com/sotr_game 
• on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/shadowoftheroad/ 
• on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/sotr_game/

[b]Q: Is there any official knowledge base available for Shadow of the Road?[/b]
*A:* Yes, we recently set up a Fandom wiki that is available here https://shadowoftheroad.fandom.com/wiki/Shadow_of_the_Road

[b]Q: Why is the release date so distant?[/b]
*A:* You haven't seen all our ideas yet! Jokes aside though - we have to expand our team a bit more, and we would like to make SotR not only content-rich but also (and primarily) fun to play so that takes time. A lot of it.

notes.title: New locations, quests & team management
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/62d00c03092f0935f359b68f0639487a989f8779.jpg[/img]

The last ten weeks have been incredibly hard on us. We have been working on an update that is going to concern exploration and the narrative. 

[b]## Narrative updates [/b]

We have successfully managed to complete our first gameplay that is over an hour long and consists not only of enemy encounters and skirmishes, but is also heavily focused on the story.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/f1453478e34e23aa569488310c6430eb981da57f.jpg[/img]

We have added a dialogue system that gives us different options on how to progress on multiple levels. The aspect that we are especially proud of is the fact that any member of your team can take part in a conversation - not just Satoru, the protagonist. As mentioned before, the choices you make will influence different aspects of the story - including relationships between characters and the narrative in general.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/5fab16fabd9b66d02b17b2582b2c93ffa35d5d95.jpg[/img]

We have also designed alternative paths that can be taken by the player and these actually influence much more than just dialogues. The mechanics we use in combat, the enemies we encounter, and the way the story unfolds are all going to depend on which path we decide to follow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/7819be7f0ba21213d1164d069656e3165a69b1c9.jpg[/img]


[b]## Barks  [/b]

We want to make sure that all characters are aware of their surroundings and that they're not indifferent to everything happening around them. Barks are something that we want to use to cover this aspect in Shadow of the Road. The characters are going to make comments on different events, locations etc. in real-time, helping us understand their views and personalities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/7ece8c181e16e62559f9937151fef3b2f36cf20e.jpg[/img]

[b]## New locations - sneak peek[/b]

Beautiful hills

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/209ac05c20343b4ac5f02c111b9769c1956c1d24.jpg[/img]

Graveyard and a shrine

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/ed4a6961b13e46ea93fa8c45703bfc9214ea1d4f.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/7479e60a41212be4c3846f13d52afa721c43c8be.jpg[/img]

Caves

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/26a54b254cb9e6f0b87c466e4f963bc6465d50c3.jpg[/img]

[b]## Inventory etc.[/b]

Here's our first ever look at the inventory. What's important is that weapons can be enchanted to add some new features, a crafting system is also going to be in place and every character is going to have a separate equipment stash that is going to be manageable outside of combat.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/0fe4e9d0b7111354c4e51bb92bf847684c11885a.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/e9117389b23b49bf69245a78bc51f2c2ad3478e8.jpg[/img]

[h2]
[b]## New Mechanics[/b][/h2]

[h3][b]# resurrection[/b][/h3]

It's better to stay alive if you have the choice. Luckily not everything is lost - as long as at least one of your team members is alive during combat, you should mostly be fine. Of course the characters that have been knocked out get brought back after the battle, but we have a very special revive mechanic that we're planning to share with you in the next update.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/RK4lpcv9T1G5LQjnbn/giphy.gif[/img]

[h3][b]# opportunity attack[/b][/h3]

This is a passive skill called Opportunity Attack. Exiting any of the red fields will result in the opponent performing an extra free attack. This is a penalty for disengaging from combat with some of the melee foes. The visual info & feedback from such actions is still in development.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/dZjN3fruXNLa2Fvrzf/source.gif[/img]

notes.title: New creatures & exploration mode update
notes.content:
Hey there! We have a special treat for you today that we hope you're going to enjoy. This is the first entry of a development update series in which we would like to highlight some of the things that we are currently working on. Please tell us if you enjoy such condensed posts and let us know if you would like to know more about any of these topics!

[h2]Kuchiberashi[/h2]
A newborn sacrificed by its parents, now acting as an ally for a more powerful entity. Constantly looking for something to eat. The creation itself has been inspired by different manifestations in the Japanese folklore but we decided to take a slightly different approach and create something unique for our game and setting.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/KEBFvYGexsq6Mb7Wui/source.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/a9bbe34b56ba798283fa5fdbe273871a97c62894.png[/img]

[h2]Exploration mode[/h2]
We've prototyped two separate control systems for wandering around in-game Japan.

One with direct control (using WSAD and a mouse):
[previewyoutube=C4xQvJfh8oA;full][/previewyoutube]

Another one based on the "Hand of God" (point & click) type of controls: 
[previewyoutube=qctoBfLyXAI;full][/previewyoutube]

Which one do you prefer? Be sure to leave a comment below or discuss it on our [url=http://bit.ly/3aNQKYq]Discord Server[/url].

[h2]Genkurō[/h2]
We do realize that white foxes are special entities in the Japanese folklore and are usually associated with the [i]kami Inari[/i] responsible for fertility, rice, tea and sake. However, our Genkurō is a spiritual guide that has more in common with the general concept of [i]kitsune[/i] - an intelligent being with paranormal abilities. You can be sure that even though his role is not clear throughout the beginning of the story he's definitely going to surprise you more than once.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35994584/ca0531d1cbe24dd6f7527b52140985c0dd4623b2.jpg[/img]

[h2]Kamaitachi[/h2]
It's finally time to present another yōkai - you met Jorōgumo some time ago and you were even able to view parts of gameplay featuring this strange arachnid entity. Kamaitachi however is a yōkai tied to our protagonist Satoru. Based on Japanese folklore Kamaitachi is a weasel-like entity with blades growing out of its arms. Kamaitachi is swift, light and usually associated with wind. Therefore we chose to include some smoke and wind currents in the design as well to bring out its magical nature even more.
